documents.text:
From:             MBBrangan@protonmail.com
To:               Marlayna Doell
Subject:          [External_Sender] Holtec"s problem at Palisades and lack of public process
Date:             Thursday, October 8, 2026 2:28:24 PM
Attachments:      ATT00001.txt


To Marlayna Doell, Project Manager, Operating Radiation Licensing Branch 3
Marlayna.Doell@nrc.gov

Re: https://www.nrc.gov/docs/ML2627/ML26275A214.pdf and
https://www.nrc.gov/docs/ML2627/ML26273A469.pdf

October 8, 2026

Dear Ms Doell,

I'm writing to express dismay at the lack of public process for the uniquely troubling drop of an
irradiated fuel assembly into a reactor vessel by Holtec at Palisades.

Though I realize that Executive Order 14300 instructed NRC to essentially 'rubber stamp' any
request from a nuclear corporation no matter what the situation is, the response to this particularly
egregious accident must be to protect workers and the public, not to allow more hasty moves that
might exacerbate the problem.  

Please realize that you personally have a responsibility to morally respond to this. Holtec must not
be allowed to continue to act without sensible safety measures and careful consideration of how
to next deal with this problem.  

The public is underwriting this travesty via the billions in Federal and state support paid to Holtec
for its attempted restart of this already long unmaintained and deficient nuclear reactor. We must
be kept informed and allowed to have independent experts participate in a public facing process
regarding this situation. Please don't allow Holtec's rushed mismanagement to continue. This is
yet another in a long string of Holtec's mistakes that can adversely affect our public health and
welfare at Palisades.

Thanks for your consideration,
Mary Beth Brangan


Mary Beth Brangan
Producer/Director
SOS - The San Onofre Syndrome: Nuclear Power's Legacy
